title: An Update on Tunbridge Wells & Rusthall Commons: Bid Status & Estate Remarketing
author: The Friends of Tunbridge Wells & Rusthall Commons
photo_credit: Photo: Kelly Wilcox • March for the Commons (21 March 2026)
summary: Following our initial April charitable bid to buy the Commons, Targetfollow has remarketed the land as part of a wider portfolio including the Upper Pantiles. While a different proposition, this opens new opportunities to negotiate securing the Commons freehold separately.
body:
Following the Friends’ charitable bid to acquire Tunbridge Wells and Rusthall Commons earlier this year, we are now able to share a comprehensive update on the latest position regarding the freehold land.

As our community of supporters will know, the Friends submitted a formal charitable bid for the Commons in April 2026. This bid followed an extraordinary and heartfelt response from local residents, families, and civic groups, resulting in more than 3,000 individual financial pledges registered with the charity.

Unfortunately, our initial bid was not accepted by the vendor, Targetfollow. There remained a significant gap between the Friends’ valuation assessment—which strictly reflects the fact that registered common land carries zero residential development rights under the 1890 Tunbridge Wells Improvement Act—and the vendor’s commercial expectations.

Targetfollow has subsequently announced that the Commons are being remarketed as part of a wider commercial portfolio that includes the Upper Pantiles, marketed through BNP Paribas Real Estate. While this represents a significantly different commercial proposition from the individual lot originally offered, it may also create distinct, new opportunities for the Friends to secure the Commons separately. We have already initiated constructive exploratory discussions and will continue to engage directly with prospective purchasers where appropriate.
